note: Every layer shipped in assets/data plus the Festival Walk 3D app data. Features counted from the file itself. Floor plate heights are schematic (5.5 m storey, 2x vertical exaggeration). The G floor is set to Tat Chee Avenue (達之路) at the junction where it meets the mall - 33.0 m measured from Esri WorldElevation3D Terrain3D - and the podium is a schematic foundation mass, not measured architectural heights. | 2026-11-05: added HK Steep Slopes >30 deg - 33,231 polygons of ground steeper than 30 degrees (113.29 km2 = 10.09% of land), the five-class slope raster at 20 m, the maximum-slope raster, and the two-panel map. Slope is the MAXIMUM gradient within each 20 m cell, not the mean: 22,700 recorded incidents sit in cells whose mean slope is under 30 degrees but whose max is over it, so a mean threshold would erase a fifth of the evidence. Area reconciliation error 0.0 m2, 0 invalid geometries.  | 2026-11-13: added HK Low-Lying Land under 5 m - the land in Hong Kong below 5 m above the Principal Datum, 60.58 km2 = 5.43% of the land, as 106 cleaned patches, all 9,060 patches, a binary 5 m raster and the map. The source DTM codes the sea as 0 m, so the land mask is essential; it is built from the OSM Hong Kong boundary relation 20044132 AND the DTM's positive elevation, and gives 1,116.0 km2 of land against a true 1,106 km2.

files.notes: 7 translucent floor plates (MTR..2/F) plus a translucent podium. files.title: Festival Walk vertical circulation, 3D (lifts / escalators / stairs / ramps)
files.notes: 29 genuine floor-to-floor connectors, separated from the 48 flat site surfaces using the CSDI FeatureType domain and Gradient field. Each connector's two floors are resolved by matching its ends against the published floor networks (a connector's ends land at 0.00 m from the floor it serves). Carries floor_from, floor_to, mode (link / shaft / incline) and rise_m. The app draws each connector with a different z on each vertex, so lifts are vertical shafts and escalators slope between floors.

files.title: Steep slope polygons - ground steeper than 30 degrees
files.notes: 33,231 polygons of ground exceeding a 30 degree gradient, 113.29 km2 = 10.09% of Hong Kong's land area (1,122.26 km2). Slope is the MAXIMUM gradient within each 20 m cell (Horn's method) from the LandsD 5 m DTM, because 22,700 recorded incidents sit in cells whose mean slope is under 30 degrees but whose max is over it. 8-connectivity, so corner-touching steep cells merge into one hillside. Area reconciliation error 0.0 m2, 0 invalid geometries. EPSG:4326 (GeoJSON is always lon/lat); the area above is measured in EPSG:2326 (HK1980).

files.title: Maximum slope raster (20 m)
files.notes: Maximum gradient within each 20 m cell, degrees, from the LandsD 5 m DTM (Horn's method). 3187 x 2400 at 20 m, float32, EPSG:2326 (HK1980), nodata -9999.

files.title: Steep slopes of Hong Kong - two-panel map
files.notes: Panel A: five slope classes with 40,000 of the 124,020 recorded landslide incidents overprinted. Panel B: the >30 degree polygons alone over the gentler land, with the six largest regions labelled by area. Scale bar, north arrow and source line. Text overlap and off-canvas checks both pass at zero; a pixel probe confirms all five classes are rendered.

files.title: Hong Kong land below 5 m elevation
files.notes: The 106 contiguous patches of Hong Kong whose ground level is below 5 m above the Hong Kong Principal Datum, 60.58 km2 = 5.43% of the land. Patches under 0.05 km2 are dropped for readability (they hold 10.68 km2 between them and are in the all-patches layer). Each feature carries its area in km2 and hectares, its centre point in lon/lat, and the mean, minimum and maximum elevation within the patch. EPSG:4326 (GeoJSON is always lon/lat, RFC 7946); the areas are measured in EPSG:2326 (HK1980) and the reprojection changes them by 0.000000 km2. The sea is coded 0 m in the source DTM, so the land mask is essential - without it the query returns the whole ocean.

files.title: Hong Kong land below 5 m elevation - every patch
files.notes: All 9,060 contiguous patches of low-lying land, including the slivers under 0.05 km2 that the cleaned layer drops. The two layers together hold the same 60.58 km2. EPSG:4326 (RFC 7946).

files.title: Low-lying land raster (5 m)
files.notes: Binary raster on the 5 m DTM grid, 12751 x 9601 at 5 m, EPSG:2326 (HK1980): 1 = land below 5 m, 0 = everything else. 2,423,036 cells = 60.58 km2. Deflate-compressed GeoTIFF.

files.title: Low-lying land patch table

files.title: Hong Kong land below 5 m - the low-lying land map

files.title: Low-lying land under 5 m - method note
files.notes: The method note: why the DTM's sea-as-0 m coding makes a land mask essential, the six land boundaries that were tested and how each one fails, the OSM Hong Kong boundary that was used, the acceptance test against Hong Kong's true land area and against 48 named places, the ArcGIS Pro instructions, and the known limits.

scripts.description: Fetch and validate the VIIRS night-lights nights. Rejects blank (all-zero) rasters by CONTENT, not by HTTP status, because GIBS returns 200 with an empty raster for unserved dates.
Score the 41 campsites on darkness, access, facilities and horizon. Asserts every factor is populated, no score is NaN, and that the access term yields more than 20 distinct values.

Build the two-panel figure. Checks text overlap and off-canvas text BEFORE saving, then verifies the rendered pixels over the bright city, the dark country and the dark sea each match the source raster value at that location.
Copy the outputs into the repo layout and verify each shipped file.
Extend this manifest with the camping entries and verify every entry against the file on disk.
Fetch the OSM coastline via /map, with adaptive bbox splitting on HTTP 400 and backoff on HTTP 429. The coastline is an orientation overlay only - it is NOT used as a land mask.
Merge the bbox-clipped coastline fragments into complete ways. Merging by way id instead of node sequence keeps only the last fragment of any way crossing a box boundary, which guts the coastline.
Flood-fill the land from the sea over a rasterised coastline. Kept for the record: it fails where the coastline is not closed, which is why the shipped map applies no land mask at all.
Record the build scripts in this manifest and verify each one against the file on disk.

Download the published script and its two inputs into a fresh temporary directory and run the build there with only the environment variables set. Proves the repo copy works off the author's machine, which is the thing a student actually needs.
Downloads the 693 nightly VIIRS rasters from NASA GIBS
The main corrected analysis: land mask, distance control, structure exclusion, within-night contrast, seasonal double difference, vessel validation and the per-area breakdown
The active-night list and the spatial description of the largest night
Leave-one-year-out, leave-one-night-out and threshold sensitivity
Tests whether the GIBS product changed around 2023
Separates fixed structures from moving boats by nights-per-cell
The dark-moon test on the transient bright cells
Builds the corrected four-panel figure
The figure gate: text overlap, off-canvas and pixel probes
Derives the flood mechanism for all 267 locations from the coastline, the 5 m DTM, the drainage network and the catchments
Builds the flood-mechanism figure
The figure gate: text overlap, off-canvas and pixel probes
Fetches the supporting DSD, WSD and CEDD layers with pagination and asserted final counts
Cross-checks the 226 scraped blockage titles against DSD's own published PDF
Builds the flood-prone-areas overview map
The variance decomposition: how much of the night-to-night swing is nuisance, and a comparison of four ways to average it
Refresh the scripts section of MANIFEST.json after a cross-cutting code change: updates bytes and sha256 for every script entry, and checks that the files section holds no code
Downloads the LandsD Whole HK DTM 5 m and converts the 302 MB ESRI ASCII grid to a fast .npy array for sampling
Helpers for writing RFC 7946 GeoJSON: reproject EPSG:2326 to lon/lat, strip the crs member, measure area in the projected CRS, and gate the result
Reprojects the three landslide GeoJSON layers to EPSG:4326 and removes the crs member, cross-checked against the independently produced WGS 84 sibling and by an area reconciliation in EPSG:2326
Fetches the 21 layers behind the flash-flood and storm-surge factors from the CSDI FeatureServers, paginated at 3,000 features per request
Fetches the COMPLETE GEO raingauge daily record (1984-2026, 1,126,191 rows). The main fetch takes only 2020-onward to keep the download small, but that subset hides the territory's rainfall record
Joins the complete rainfall record with the gauge coordinates: the full file has no geometry and its attributes sit under 'attributes', not 'properties'
Horn 3x3 slope and D8 flow accumulation from the LandsD 5 m DTM, and the per-location terrain factors
Scores the 267 locations on the six flash-flood and five storm-surge factors, with the weights stated in the method note
Builds the three-panel flood-causes figure
The figure gate: text overlap, off-canvas text, marker-under-text, pixel probes on the saved PNG, and the panel C table checked against the source layer
Fetch the mean diurnal tidal range at each HKO tide station from the live high/low tide CSVs. The CSVs have no high/low marker column, so the tides are separated by the local-extremum test.

Convert the cached 3D Pedestrian Network from the ArcGIS 'geojson' output format to RFC 7946 GeoJSON: 'attributes' -> 'properties', ESRI 'paths' -> LineString/MultiLineString, and 'type': 'Feature' added to every feature. The ArcGIS service calls its own output format 'geojson' but it is not GeoJSON.

Publish the low-lying land layer into the repo: reproject the EPSG:2326 polygons to lon/lat AT THE SHIPPING BOUNDARY, write them gzipped, copy the raster, the table, the map and the note, then read every shipped file back and assert the feature counts, the absence of a crs member and that the coordinates are lon/lat. The area is measured in EPSG:2326 before and after the reprojection and must agree.

Add the low-lying land entries to the MANIFEST, reading the feature counts and sha256 FROM THE SHIPPED FILES, extending the manifest in place and then re-reading every entry to confirm it still matches disk.

Fetch the OpenStreetMap coastline for Hong Kong from the OSM API in a tiled grid, caching every chunk on disk. Overpass was unavailable, so this uses api/0.6/map directly. The API answers HTTP 400 when a bbox is too large, so a failing tile is halved and retried down to four levels. A tile that still fails is reported loudly and the run exits non-zero, because a hole in the coastline leaks the land mask.
Turn the cached OSM tiles into one coastline file and report how the ways chain into rings.

Build the Hong Kong land mask from the OSM boundary relations 20044132 and 913110 chained with the Guangdong-Hong Kong border ways and the coastline ways, intersected with the DTM's positive elevation, then verify it against named land and water places and against Hong Kong's true land area.
Write the low-lying land deliverables: the binary GeoTIFF, the cleaned and the all-patches GeoJSON, and the patch table.
Draw the low-lying land map and check the text overlap and the off-canvas text BEFORE saving.
Package the deliverables for delivery: copy them to disk, build a ZIP under the 50 MB limit, then extract it and re-read every file.

Fetch the OSM Hong Kong boundary's member ways BY ID, so the land mask can be rebuilt from a fresh clone. The tiled coastline fetch does not carry the ways that run along the Shenzhen land border. Use /way/<id>/full, NOT /ways?ways=... - the bulk endpoint returns the ways with only <nd ref> and no node coordinates, so the geometry cannot be resolved from it. The fetched files keep the node coordinates.
